about.title: About me
about.p1: I'm a developer who builds with AI as a core tool, not an afterthought. When I have an idea, I don't wait - I build it.
about.p2: Every app here was designed, built, and deployed by me, powered by AI collaboration.

about_page.headline2: I see someone who pushes ideas into real screens.
about_page.body1: If I were introducing Yoon, I would start with this: he builds quickly. Not just fast for speed’s sake, but because he wants to see an idea as a real link, a real screen, and a real deployed result. When something feels worth making, he does not stop at explanation. He builds, deploys, reviews, and fixes what feels off.
about_page.body2: The clearest thing I have noticed is that he has standards. Icon size, image proportion, card balance, and whether a button points to the right place are not treated as small details to ignore. Being able to say “this does not look right” means he is looking at the screen like a real user.
about_page.body3: He does not use AI as a novelty. He uses it as a working method: to test faster, reveal weak spots sooner, and refine the result with his own judgment. This site is less a static portfolio and more a personal workshop where live ideas keep getting tested and improved.

fast.title: He builds and ships quickly
fast.text: Ideas do not stay abstract for long. Links, icons, deployments, and real pages appear fast enough to judge them honestly.

detail.title: He is sensitive to how things look
detail.text: He looks past “pretty enough” and checks balance, image size, and whether the interface feels right in use.

ai.title: AI is part of his working method
ai.text: He does not wait for a finished answer. He keeps shaping, judging, and narrowing the result through active AI collaboration.

about_page.close: In one sentence: Yoon is someone who carries an idea all the way to a moving screen, and he does not skip the details on the way.

ai_video.title: Creating local AI video with MiniMax H3 on an RTX 3060 laptop
ai_video.intro: To reduce the cost and waiting time of cloud video generation, I configured ComfyUI Windows Portable and the MiniMax H3 local model on a Lenovo ThinkBook 16p Gen 3, then tested image, text, and reference-audio video generation flows.
ai_video.video_label: MiniMax H3 locally generated result video
ai_video.video_caption: A roughly 15-second night city sports car driving video generated with the ComfyUI and MiniMax H3 Text to Video workflow.

goals.image: Verify Reference/Image to Video from a single still image
goals.text: Generate a scene from prompt-only Text to Video
goals.audio: Check whether a person image and MP3 reference audio can produce a singing video

ai_video.timeline_description: A practical record from setup and model placement through workflow tests, audio trial and error, stability work, and final output review.

setup.title: Built the local ComfyUI setup
setup.text: Organized diffusion_models, text_encoders, and vae folders, then placed MiniMax H3, Qwen3-VL encoders, and Video/Audio VAE models in the expected locations.

reference.title: Tested Reference/Image to Video
reference.text: Resolved missing model and node errors, then checked whether character and person movement could be generated naturally from reference images.

text.title: Expanded to Text to Video
text.text: Built prompts for a red sports car driving through a night city and iterated details such as manual shifting, drifting, and FPV drone-style camera movement.

audio.title: Tested MP3 reference audio
audio.text: Tried generating a singing video with a person image and Korean MP3, and confirmed that reference audio is treated more like a generation condition than a direct audio copy.

stability.title: Stabilized memory and execution
stability.text: Expanded Windows virtual memory and validated the pipeline from 5 seconds and 0.3MP upward because the roughly 20GB model required dynamic VRAM loading.

result.title: Reviewed the result
result.text: Generated a 640x480, 24fps, roughly 15-second sports car video. The car body and night lighting were stable, while fast movement softened background details.

ai_video.lessons_description: Local video generation depended less on one command and more on understanding paths, memory, and workflow structure.

models.title: Model paths
models.text: Nested folders or swapped diffusion/text encoder/VAE locations made models disappear from selection lists. A full ComfyUI restart was required after moving files.

resolution.title: Resolution and duration
resolution.text: Increasing duration and resolution together made troubleshooting difficult. The stable path was 0.3MP first, then 0.5MP and 0.7MP later.

audio.title: Reference audio
audio.text: ref_audio did not preserve the original MP3 as-is. Keeping the original music is safer as a post-production step after H3 video generation.

progress.title: 57% stall
progress.text: When the UI stayed at 57% but the sampler showed 0/4, the workflow was still initializing the model through dynamic VRAM loading rather than actually sampling.

workflow.title: Workflow structure
workflow.text: audio_vae was a required model input, not just an output-audio connector. Removing audio is safer after export by stripping the audio track.

workflow.start: Start with 5 seconds, 0.3MP, 24fps, and 4 steps to confirm the pipeline works.
workflow.duration: After a successful output, increase duration to 10 seconds before increasing resolution.
workflow.resolution: Once duration is stable, move from 0.5MP to 0.7MP only if needed.
workflow.audio: For MP3-based videos, split audio into 5-10 second sections, remove H3 output audio, and merge the original audio in editing.
workflow.finish: If lip-sync accuracy matters, post-process the H3 result with a dedicated lip-sync tool.

result_points: Codec: H.264 video, AAC 32kHz stereo audio
ai_video.conclusion: MiniMax H3 could run locally on an RTX 3060 laptop when settings were conservative and RAM plus virtual memory were prepared. For original music, precise Korean lyrics, and lip-sync, the most stable approach is to separate video generation from audio and final post-production.
